descriptionChirho: Green plant growth, grass, or herbage, typically used as an image of transience and frailty of human life (Isa 40:6-8 'all flesh is grass,' Ps 103:15, 2 Kgs 19:26). Consistently rendered: Spanish 'hierba,' Arabic عشب (ushb), Korean 풀 (pul), Hindi घास (ghas), Swahili 'majani/nyasi.' All three clusters represent the same botanical referent — bare noun 'grass,' comparative 'like grass,' and construct 'grass of' — with no semantic differentiation, only grammatical variation in definiteness and prepositional framing.
